pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/worker.rs:1657 The lease reaper turns "we stopped hearing from this job" into a permanent failure and runs the normal failure finalize (callback and terminal triggers), so whatever watches the fleet cannot tell a job the sweeper declared dead from one that reported its own error.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/worker.rs:1657 The sweeper's verdict goes out as an ordinary failure through finalize. There is no 'lost' outcome separate from a self-reported failure.
crates/server/src/worker.rs:24 One global slot cap is enforced at the single claim loop, and a per-app cap sits on top of it (blocked_apps). Slots are released through an RAII permit.
crates/server/src/worker.rs:1297 The attempt number works as a generation token. A stale incarnation that was reset or reaped cannot act for the job it lost.
crates/server/src/worker.rs:284 The drain suspends in-flight jobs to their checkpoint under the same job id instead of killing them. The suspend is told apart from a user cancel (CancelKind).
crates/server/src/worker.rs:306 Whatever is still running at the drain deadline gets the same recovery verdict as the boot sweep, and the requeued, failed and skipped counts are reported separately.
crates/server/src/worker.rs:64 Local runs are in-process tokio tasks, so process exit is the reaper and there is no external substrate to converge.

pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:1890 reap_stale and the boot sweep pass a silent job to fail() with only a Text reason, so the row ends up queued or failed with requeue_reason and cause_kind identical to a self-reported text failure, and the sweeper's inference can be told from a reported error only by parsing the prose of the error column.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:1890 The tier-two sweeper writes a self-reported-failure state, not an honest 'lost' state.
crates/core/src/job.rs:54 The vocabulary is closed and single-sourced, but its terminal set has no 'lost' member, so 'lost' and 'failed' are merged.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:4546 An unrecognized stored status is an error, never defaulted to a plausible state.

crates/core/src/job.rs:13 'waiting' is a first-class parked state: the slot is released and the identity kept. Resume goes back to queued, and the pending input survives in input_request/resumed_input.
crates/core/src/job.rs:80 target_key declares collision domains and the claim keeps them disjoint.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1823 The boot sweep and the lease reaper share one verdict function. It is bounded, idempotent, and reports per-class counts.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:876 Executors claim by polling outbound, with an allow-list. The lease holder is stamped in the same statement that claims the job, and heartbeats are fenced on executor_id.
